mainTopic: Reading the משנה of the borrowed-and-rented cow as a partial admission, so רבא's rule מתוך שאינו יכול לישבע משלם applies, both in the plain reading and by רמי בר חמא
overview: The גמרא explains why our משנה makes the borrower pay when he says 'I don't know.' It reads the משנה as a case where the borrower admits part of the claim (מודה במקצת). That admission means he owes an oath, but he cannot swear about something he doesn't know. So by רבא's rule, מתוך שאינו יכול לישבע משלם, he must pay. The גמרא sets up the cases with more cows: two cows for the רישא and three for the סיפא. In each case the borrower admits one cow and is unsure about another. Then the גמרא reads the משנה again by רמי בר חמא, who holds that a שומר swears only if he both denies part and admits part. That needs one more cow to deny, so the רישא becomes three cows and the סיפא four. The four-cow case begins here, and the borrower's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא's rule: if he cannot swear, he pays
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that someone who admits fifty out of a claimed hundred, and says he does not know about the rest, must pay the whole amount, because he cannot take the oath he owes.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא says: Someone claims, 'You have a hundred of mine,' and the other answers, 'You only have fifty with me, and about the rest I don't know.' Since he cannot swear, he pays.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא's ruling to support its point that our משנה can be read as a case of partial admission. It is not a case of a plain 'I don't know.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Admitting part of a claim (מודה במקצת) makes a person owe a Torah oath that he does not owe the rest. Here the defendant cannot swear, because he honestly does not know. So רבא rules he must pay the rest instead. This rule is what lets the גמרא explain the משנה without deciding the plain 'I don't know' case.

keyTerms.meaning: A sum of one hundred זוז (dinars)
The other one (the defendant)
Since he cannot take the oath, he must pay
One who admits part of a claim and so owes an oath on the rest

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT the case of someone who simply says 'I don't know' about the whole claim. Here he admits part, and that admission is what creates the oath he cannot take.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the key to the whole explanation that follows. Every case the גמרא builds next is designed to fit this pattern.

phrases.english: As Rava says:
"I have a hundred in your hand,"
and the other one says:
You have in my hand only fifty,
and the rest, I do not know.
Since he is unable to swear,
he pays.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the answer just given before this section: the משנה is read as a case where רבא's rule applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who admits part of a claim and says he does not know about the rest must pay, because he cannot take the required oath.

steps.title: Finding partial admission in the משנה: two cows and three cows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה's first clauses can be read as cases of two cows, and its last clause as a case of three cows. This creates a partial admission.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can find it: the first clause with two cows, and the last clause with three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא announces how it will fit the משנה into רבא's rule. This line sets up the next steps, which spell out the details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only one cow, the borrower could not admit just part of the claim. By imagining more cows, he can admit to one and say 'I don't know' about another. That is exactly the partial-admission pattern רבא described.

keyTerms.meaning: You can find it (a way the case can work)
The first clause of the משנה
The last clause of the משנה

phrases.english: You can find it: the first clause with two
phrases.notes: 'It' means a case of partial admission inside our משנה; 'two' and 'three' are cows.

phrases.english: and the last clause with three.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ רֵישָׁא בִּשְׁתַּיִם וְסֵיפָא בְּשָׁלֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבא's rule to the משנה by setting up the cases with more than one cow.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case (אוקימתא) as one with multiple cows
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to show that a plain 'I don't know' makes the borrower pay.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a partial admission with several cows, so the borrower pays only because of רבא's rule.

steps.title: The owner's claim in the two-cow case
steps.stepSummary: The owner claims he gave two cows, part of the time as a loan and part as a rental, and that both died during the loan time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first clause with two: the owner said, 'I gave you two cows, half the day as a loan and half the day as a rental.' Or: 'one day as a loan and one day as a rental.' 'And both died during the loan time.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the owner's claim for the first clauses of the משנה. It matches the משנה's two time-splits: half a day each, or one day each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שואל (borrower) must pay even when an animal dies by accident, but a שוכר (renter) does not. So the owner claims both cows died during the loan time, which would make the borrower pay for both. That sets the stage for the borrower to admit only part.

keyTerms.meaning: Borrowing (free use, borrower is fully responsible)
Renting (paid use, renter is less responsible)
Half of the day
Or alternatively
At the time of, during

phrases.english: The first clause with two:
that he said to him:
phrases.notes: The owner is speaking to the person who took the cows.

phrases.english: I handed two cows over to you,
half the day as a loan,
and half the day as a rental.
Or alternatively:
one day as a loan,
and one day as a rental,
and both of them died during the loan time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the details of the two-cow case announced in Step 2.
steps.terutzMaskana: The owner claims full payment for two cows that he says died during the loan time.

steps.title: The borrower admits one cow and is unsure about the other, so he pays
steps.stepSummary: The borrower admits one cow died during the loan time but does not know about the second. This is a partial admission, so by רבא's rule he pays for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: The borrower answered: 'One, yes, it died during the loan time. The other, I don't know whether it died during the loan time or during the rental time.' Since he cannot swear, he pays.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the two-cow case with the borrower's answer. It shows how רבא's rule makes him pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By admitting one cow, the borrower is a מודה במקצת and owes an oath about the second cow. He cannot swear, because he says he does not know. So he must pay for the second cow too, which is why the משנה says he is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: The borrower
One (of them)
Yes
And the other one
I do not know

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'I don't know' is explained as a partial admission involving two cows. The borrower pays because of מתוך שאינו יכול לישבע משלם, not because a plain 'I don't know' always makes someone pay.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explanation lets the משנה fit even the view that a plain 'I don't know' does not make someone pay.

phrases.english: And the borrower said to him:
One — yes,
it died during the loan time,
and the other — I don't know
whether it died during the loan time
or whether it died during the rental time,
for since he is unable to swear, he pays.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-cow case with the borrower's partial admission and applies רבא's rule from Step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the first clauses of the משנה, the borrower pays for both cows because he admitted one and cannot swear about the other.

steps.title: The last clause: the owner claims three cows, two of them borrowed
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא of the משנה is a case of three cows. Two were borrowed and one was rented. The owner claims the two borrowed cows are the ones that died.
steps.simpleTranslation: The last clause is a case of three cows. The owner says: I gave you three cows, two as a loan and one as a rental, and the two loaned ones died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the משנה's last clause, using three cows. This step only gives the owner's claim. The borrower's answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 2 the גמרא said the earlier clauses use two cows and the last clause uses three. Here it builds the three-cow case. Two cows were a loan (for these the borrower must pay even if they die naturally) and one was a rental (he does not pay if it dies naturally). The owner says both loaned cows died, so the borrower owes for two.

keyTerms.meaning: The last clause of the משנה
Borrowing; a borrower pays even if the animal dies naturally
Renting; a renter does not pay if the animal dies naturally
Two

phrases.english: And the last clause is a case of three cows:
where the owner said to him:
I gave you three cows,
two as a loan and one as a rental,
and those two loaned ones are the ones that died,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the two-cow case (steps 3-4) to the three-cow case promised in step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case setup so the משנה's last clause creates a partial admission
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It is not clear how the last clause could involve a partial admission and an oath
steps.terutzMaskana: With three cows, the owner can claim that two specific borrowed cows died

steps.title: The borrower admits one borrowed cow died but does not know about the other
steps.stepSummary: The borrower admits one borrowed cow died. About the second dead cow, he does not know if it was borrowed or rented. Since he cannot swear, he pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: The borrower says: Yes, one loaned cow died. About the other, I do not know. Maybe the loaned one died and the living one is the rented one, or maybe the rented one died and the living one is the loaned one. Since he cannot swear, he pays.
steps.whatsHappening: The borrower answers the owner. He admits part of the claim and says 'I don't know' about the rest, so רבא's rule from step 1 makes him pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner claimed two borrowed cows. The borrower admits one, which is a partial admission, so he owes an oath on the rest. But he says he does not know whether the cow still alive is the borrowed one or the rented one. He cannot swear about something he does not know, so he must pay.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not know
The one that is still standing, still alive
Since he cannot take the oath, he pays (רבא's rule)

steps.whatToRemember: By רבא, the three-cow סיפא works the same way as the two-cow case: admit part, don't know the rest, can't swear, so pay.

phrases.english: and the borrower said to him:
Yes, one of the loaned cows died,
the other one, I do not know
whether the loaned one died
and the one still alive is the rented one,
or whether the rented one died
and this one still alive is the loaned one,
and since he cannot take the oath, he pays.
phrases.notes: This is רבא's rule from step 1.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ שׁוֹאֵל: אִין, חֲדָא דִּשְׁאֵילָה מֵתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the borrower's response to the owner's claim in step 5 and applies רבא's rule
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's last clause fits רבא: a partial admission with 'I don't know' about the rest makes the borrower pay.

steps.title: Reading the משנה by רמי בר חמא's view
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא holds that a שומר only swears if he denies part of the claim and admits part. By his view, the רישא is a case of three cows and the סיפא a case of four.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by רמי בר חמא, who says the four kinds of guardians need both a partial denial and a partial admission, you can find the first clause with three cows and the last clause with four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second way to read the משנה, following רמי בר חמא. This step sets up the plan, and the next steps fill in the details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first reading, admitting part of the claim was enough to require an oath. רמי בר חמא holds that a שומר swears only if he also denies part. So every case needs one more cow, one to deny. That makes the רישא three cows and the סיפא four.

keyTerms.meaning: The four kinds of guardians: unpaid, paid, renter, borrower
Denying part of the claim
Admitting part of the claim
You can find it, meaning the case can be set up this way
The first clause of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two readings. The first reading uses only a partial admission. רמי בר חמא requires a partial admission and also a partial denial, which is why each case needs an extra cow. רבא's rule (can't swear, so pay) applies in both readings.

phrases.english: And according to רמי בר חמא, who says:
the four kinds of guardians need
a denial of part and an admission of part,
phrases.notes: He means: only then do they have to swear.

phrases.english: you can find the first clause with three cows
and the last clause with four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the method of step 2, but under רמי בר חמא's stricter oath rule
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adjusts the number of cows in each case so it fits a stricter view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה might only make sense if admitting part alone is enough to require a שומר's oath
steps.terutzMaskana: By adding a cow to deny, the משנה also fits רמי בר חמא

steps.title: The first clause by רמי בר חמא: the owner claims three cows died during the loan time
steps.stepSummary: The owner says he gave three cows, half a day as a loan and half a day as a rental (or one day each), and all three died during the loan time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first clause is three cows: the owner says, I gave you three cows, half the day as a loan and half the day as a rental, or one day as a loan and one day as a rental, and all three died during the loan time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds the three-cow רישא for רמי בר חמא. This step gives only the owner's claim. The borrower's answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like step 3, each cow switches between loan time and rental time. Now there are three cows, and the owner says all three died during the loan time, so the borrower owes for all of them. The third cow gives the borrower something to deny.

keyTerms.meaning: Half of the day
Or also, alternatively
The time when the cows were on loan

phrases.english: The first clause is a case of three cows:

phrases.aramaic: דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ: שָׁלֹשׁ פָּרוֹת נָתַתִּי לְךָ,
phrases.english: where the owner said to him: I gave you three cows,
half of the day as a loan
and half of the day as a rental,
or else one day as a loan
and one day as a rental,
and all three died during the loan time,

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא בְּשָׁלֹשׁ – דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ: שָׁלֹשׁ פָּרוֹת נָתַתִּי לְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the three-cow רישא announced in step 7, using the same loan/rental timing as step 3
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two-cow setup of step 3 has nothing for the borrower to deny
steps.terutzMaskana: With three cows claimed, the borrower can deny one, admit one, and not know about one

steps.title: The borrower denies one cow, admits one, and does not know about the third
steps.stepSummary: The borrower says one cow never happened, one did die in the loan time, and he doesn't know about the third. Since he cannot swear, he pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: The borrower says: One cow, this never happened. One, yes, died during the loan time. The other, I don't know if it died during the loan time or the rental time. Since he cannot swear, he pays.
steps.whatsHappening: The borrower answers with a denial, an admission, and an 'I don't know.' This gives exactly what רמי בר חמא needs for an oath, and since he cannot swear, he pays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The denial ('this never happened') and the admission ('yes, it died in the loan time') together create the oath by רמי בר חמא's rule. But for the third cow he says 'I don't know,' so he cannot swear honestly about it. So the rule 'since he cannot swear, he pays' applies here too.

keyTerms.meaning: This never happened at all; a full denial
The other one

steps.whatToRemember: By רמי בר חמא, the רישא needs three cows: one denied, one admitted, one unknown. The 'can't swear, so pay' rule still decides the case.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the משנה can be explained even by רמי בר חמא's stricter view, just by changing how many cows are in each case. רבא's rule still decides the outcome.

phrases.english: And the borrower said to him:
One, this never happened.
phrases.notes: He is saying he never took that third cow at all; that's the denial.

phrases.english: And one, yes, it died during the loan time,
and the other one, I do not know
whether it died during the loan time
or whether it died during the rental time,
so since he cannot take the oath, he pays.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ שׁוֹאֵל: חֲדָא – לֹא הָיוּ דְבָרִים מֵעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the borrower's response to the owner's claim in step 8 and completes the רישא by רמי בר חמא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: By רמי בר חמא, the three-cow רישא gives both a denial and an admission, so an oath is owed. Since the borrower cannot swear about the unknown cow, he pays.

steps.title: The latter case involves four cows: the owner's claim
steps.stepSummary: By רמי בר חמא's view, the סיפא is a case where the owner says he gave four cows, three borrowed and one rented, and that the three borrowed ones died. The גמרא then begins to introduce the borrower's reply.
steps.simpleTranslation: The סיפא is about four cows. The owner told the borrower: 'I gave you four cows, three as a loan and one as a rental, and the three borrowed ones died.' And the borrower answered him...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is now explaining the סיפא of the משנה, as רמי בר חמא would read it, by describing the owner's claim about four cows. The last words, 'and he said to him,' set up the borrower's answer, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 7 the גמרא briefly said that for רמי בר חמא the סיפא is a four-cow case. Here it spells out that case, starting with the owner's side. The owner claims all three borrowed cows died, because the borrower is fully liable for a borrowed animal that dies.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause is a case of four (cows)
As a loan, borrowed for free
As a rental, paid for
Those (Aramaic)

steps.confusionAlert: This line repeats 'the סיפא is a case of four' from earlier. It is not a new claim. The גמרא is now actually explaining what that four-cow case looks like.

phrases.english: The latter clause is a case of four
phrases.notes: Four cows, the case mentioned briefly back in step 7.

phrases.english: where he said to him:
I gave you four cows,
three as a loan, one as a rental,
and those three that were borrowed died.
And he said to him
phrases.notes: Now the borrower is about to answer. His answer continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the three-cow רישא in steps 8-9, the גמרא now turns to the סיפא and begins defining it as a four-cow case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): the סיפא is read as involving four cows instead of three.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The three-cow סיפא from step 5 leaves the borrower nothing to deny, so it does not fit רמי בר חמא's rule that a שומר swears only when he both denies part and admits part.
steps.terutzMaskana: Adding a fourth cow makes room for a case that fits his rule. The owner claims three borrowed cows died, and the borrower's answer, coming next, will give the details.
